text:
sam: heads-up — apiserver 5xx spike in eu-central1, controller-manager requeues skyrocketing. lots of GPU pods stuck Pending/Terminating after a scale event. looks like KV reads went slow right after autoscaler bounce.

anya: saw ~45 GPU nodes stuck in Terminating state. drainage hanging on kubelet finalizers. autoscaler did a burst scale-down ~10m ago.

leo: checking cloud metrics — nat-gateway-eu-central1 connections at 93% for last 12m, NAT ephemeral port exhaustion possible. if controlplane clients can't reach etcd or kubelets we get retries -> 503s.

rachel: logs show etcd leader ping latency and kv read timeouts:
```
2026-03-20T12:28:14Z etcdserver: read request timed out: 1200ms
2026-03-20T12:28:15Z apiserver: GET /api/v1/pods 503 1.17s
2026-03-20T12:28:17Z controller-manager: requeue key default/worker-queue (backoff 2s)
```

sam: paging inc, will add notes. any quick mitigation?

anya: temporary mitigation i tried — paused cluster-autoscaler, forced remove finalizers on 8 stuck nodes, drained 3 nodes manually then cordoned. that dropped number of_PENDING pods by ~30%.

leo: bumped NAT pool to +50 ephemeral ports via cloud console (request id cf-9921) — watching for connection decline. also kicked off a small canary to avoid autoscaler burst.

rachel: after draining + NAT bump apiserver 5xx rate dropped to baseline in the last 5m. controller-manager requeues are decreasing. still seeing a couple of KV read spikes but much lower.

sre-oncall-bot: incident created: INC-2026 — APISERVER 5xx spike eu-central1. paging: @sam @anya @leo.

infra-bot: created cloud ticket CT-8842 to request NAT gateway capacity increase and review autoscaler config.

sam: next actions: 1) revert autoscaler burst settings and add cooldown, 2) follow up with cloud on NAT capacity, 3) add health check alert on etcd kv read p95 > 500ms. opening a PR for autoscaler config rollback.

anya: +1 on alert and PR. will also add a one-off runbook step for removing stuck finalizers quickly.

leo: keeping watch on metrics, will post update in 10m. :thumbsup:

rachel: summary — root likely NAT ephemeral exhaustion during autoscaler churn causing controlplane clients to time out -> etcd read spikes -> apiserver 503. mitigation successful for now, follow-ups created.

sam: thanks team — leaving this open for postmortem.
